label: prop:gram-degeneracy-blocks-connes
title: A Lipschitz seminorm with nonzero kernel has no finite Connes sup
html:
Proposition. A Lipschitz seminorm with nonzero kernel has no finite Connes sup

Let L be a Lipschitz seminorm on an algebra of observables, let \varphi and \psi be states, and let

  d(\varphi,\psi) \;=\; \sup\,\bigl\{\, |\varphi(a) - \psi(a)| \;:\; L(a) \le 1 \,\bigr\}

be the associated Connes distance. If some k satisfies L(k) = 0 while \varphi(k) \ne \psi(k), then the supremum is unbounded: for every proposed bound M there is an admissible b with |\varphi(b) - \psi(b)| > M.

The argument in one line

Homogeneity and subadditivity give L(a + tk) \le L(a) + |t|\,L(k) = L(a), so the whole line a + tk stays inside the unit ball of the seminorm, while the objective

  \varphi(a+tk) - \psi(a+tk)
  \;=\; \bigl(\varphi(a)-\psi(a)\bigr) \;+\; t\,\bigl(\varphi(k)-\psi(k)\bigr)

grows linearly in t. Choosing t large enough overshoots any bound. The distance is +\infty as posed, not a hard computation.

Stating the conclusion as "no upper bound exists" rather than "d = \infty" keeps the statement inside an ordered field, with no top element adjoined.

Why the framework runs into it

The natural candidate for a derived metric on the state space is the Gram form of the Markov trace: build a Lipschitz seminorm from it, take the Connes supremum, and read off a distance. Under convention D that route is blocked before it starts. The star form is positive semidefinite with a one-dimensional kernel --- the block killed by the row cap --- and a kernel of the form is a kernel of the seminorm. Any state pair separating that direction supplies the k above.

The obstruction is a fact about the method, and it names its own repair: quotient by the radical, or choose a different seminorm. The consequence is packaged as finite distance forces a trivial kernel, and the quotient is shown to cost nothing by the branching identity.

Under convention C the question does not arise. Every Wedderburn weight is strictly positive there, the star form is definite, and no kernel element exists to exploit. The blocker is specific to the convention that imposes the row cap.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 under convention D the star-form spectrum is 0,\, 0.752702^{\times 3},\, 4.230339: exactly one null direction, and it is the braid-symmetric one.
